title: Rising Health Costs Put New Pressure on American Workers
subtitle: Even with job-based insurance, families are paying more as medical prices continue to climb.

summary.en: Health insurance costs for American workers are rising again, creating significant financial stress for families. A new report from KFF shows that average family premiums have reached over $28,000 annually. Many employers are passing these costs on to workers, who are also facing higher deductibles. Despite having insurance, many people are skipping medical care because they cannot afford the out-of-pocket expenses. Experts warn that these costs may continue to increase throughout 2027.
summary.zh: 美國勞工的健康保險成本再次上漲，為家庭帶來巨大的財務壓力。凱瑟家庭基金會的一份新報告顯示，家庭保險的平均保費每年已超過 2 萬 8 千美元。許多雇主將這些成本轉嫁給員工，而員工同時也面臨更高的自負額。儘管擁有保險，許多人仍因無法負擔自付費用而放棄醫療照護。專家警告，這些成本在 2027 年期間可能持續增加。

paragraphs.en: For millions of Americans, having a job with health benefits no longer guarantees financial security. Recent data shows that the cost of health insurance is continuing to rise, placing a heavy burden on workers and their families. This trend is causing many to delay or avoid necessary medical treatment, even when they are officially covered by an insurance plan.
paragraphs.zh: 對數百萬美國人而言，擁有一份提供健康福利的工作，已不再是財務安全的保證。近期數據顯示，健康保險的費用持續攀升，對勞工及其家庭造成沉重負擔。這種趨勢導致許多人即便擁有保險計畫，仍選擇延後或放棄必要的醫療服務。

paragraphs.en: According to a new annual survey from KFF, a health research organization, the average cost of a family health insurance plan has now reached over $28,000 per year. While employers pay the majority of this amount, the portion that workers must cover is also increasing. The survey found that the amount employees pay toward their family coverage rose by 9% this year. Matthew Rae, an associate director at KFF, described this as a significant challenge, noting that for many families, this expense is similar to the cost of buying a new car every year.
paragraphs.zh: 根據健康研究機構凱瑟家庭基金會（KFF）的一項年度新調查，家庭健康保險計畫的平均成本現已超過每年 2 萬 8 千美元。雖然雇主負擔了這筆金額的大部分，但勞工必須分攤的部分也在增加。調查發現，員工為家庭保險支付的費用今年上漲了 9%。凱瑟家庭基金會副主任雷伊（Matthew Rae）形容這是一項重大挑戰，並指出對許多家庭來說，這筆開銷相當於每年買一輛新車的費用。

paragraphs.en: This financial pressure is not just limited to monthly payments. Many workers are also struggling with "deductibles." A deductible is a set amount of money that a patient must pay for their own medical care before the insurance company begins to pay for any services. Joseph Babbitt, a worker in Missouri, explained that while his employer covers his premiums, the high deductibles make it difficult to afford regular visits to the doctor. He noted that in the past, these costs were much lower, but today they can reach thousands of dollars, which feels very expensive for the average family.
paragraphs.zh: 這種財務壓力不僅限於每月保費。許多勞工也正為「自負額」所苦。自負額是指在保險公司開始支付任何服務費用之前，患者必須自行負擔的固定金額。密蘇里州的勞工巴比特（Joseph Babbitt）解釋說，雖然雇主幫他支付了保費，但高額的自負額讓他難以負擔定期的就醫開銷。他提到，過去這些費用低得多，但如今可能高達數千美元，對一般家庭而言負擔極為沉重。

paragraphs.en: Because of these rising costs, many people are choosing to skip care. A report from the Commonwealth Fund, a nonprofit research group, found that about 43% of workers with job-based insurance did not get the medical care they needed over the past year because of the price. Additionally, 31% of those surveyed reported having medical debt. Sara Collins, the lead author of that report, highlighted that these high costs are directly preventing people from staying healthy.
paragraphs.zh: 由於這些成本不斷上漲，許多人選擇放棄就醫。非營利研究組織聯邦基金會（Commonwealth Fund）的一份報告發現，約有 43% 擁有雇主提供保險的勞工，在過去一年中因為價格因素而未獲得所需的醫療照護。此外，31% 的受訪者表示背負醫療債務。該報告的主要作者柯林斯（Sara Collins）強調，這些高昂的成本正直接阻礙民眾維持健康。

paragraphs.en: Employers are also feeling the impact of these rising prices. According to KFF, companies are facing higher costs for the health plans they provide to their staff. To manage these expenses, many businesses are making changes. Some are choosing different insurance providers, while others are adding rules that require patients to get approval before receiving certain services. Some companies are also limiting the number of doctors and hospitals that workers can choose from. Large employers, in particular, are increasingly asking their workers to pay a larger share of the total cost to help keep the company's expenses down.
paragraphs.zh: 雇主也感受到了物價上漲的衝擊。根據凱瑟家庭基金會的資料，企業在為員工提供健康計畫時面臨更高的成本。為了控管這些支出，許多企業正在做出調整。有些選擇更換保險供應商，有些則增加規定，要求患者在接受特定服務前必須先取得核准。部分公司也限制了員工可選擇的醫生與醫院數量。大型雇主尤其傾向要求員工分攤更大比例的總成本，以協助降低公司的支出。

paragraphs.en: There are several reasons why these costs are going up. Experts point to the rising prices of hospital services and prescription drugs as major factors. Furthermore, some reports suggest that new technology, such as artificial intelligence, is being used by medical providers to change how they bill patients and insurance companies, which may be driving prices higher. The Business Group on Health, an organization representing many employers, noted that these factors are making it difficult to keep insurance affordable.
paragraphs.zh: 導致這些成本上升的原因有多種。專家指出，醫院服務與處方藥價格上漲是主要因素。此外，部分報告顯示，醫療機構正利用人工智慧等新技術來改變向患者及保險公司收費的方式，這可能進一步推高了價格。代表許多雇主的組織「健康商業團體（Business Group on Health）」指出，這些因素使得維持保險的可負擔性變得相當困難。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, the situation does not appear to be improving. Consulting firms like AON and Marsh have projected that employers could face even higher costs next year, with some estimates suggesting increases of over 8% or 9%. If these predictions are correct, it would mark several years of significant price jumps. As these costs continue to climb, the affordability of health care has become a top concern for voters and policymakers alike.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，情況似乎沒有好轉跡象。怡安集團（AON）與達信集團（Marsh）等顧問公司預測，雇主明年可能面臨更高的成本，部分估計顯示漲幅將超過 8% 或 9%。如果這些預測準確，這將標誌著連續數年的顯著價格跳漲。隨著這些成本持續攀升，醫療保健的可負擔性已成為選民與決策者共同關注的首要議題。

paragraphs.en: While some experts have noted that the rate of growth for insurance premiums is not as fast as it was in some previous years, the total cost remains very high. For the average worker, the combination of rising premiums, higher deductibles, and the general cost of living creates a difficult environment. As the country looks toward 2027, the question of how to make health care more affordable for working families remains a central issue in the United States.
paragraphs.zh: 雖然一些專家指出，保險費率的成長速度不如往年快速，但總成本依然居高不下。對於一般勞工而言，保費上漲、自負額提高以及整體生活成本的增加，共同營造了一個艱困的環境。隨著國家邁向 2027 年，如何讓受薪家庭更能負擔醫療保健，依然是美國的核心議題。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To pay for or provide financial protection against a cost or loss.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 支付（費用）；承擔（保險範圍）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（封面），這裡作動詞，指保險公司承擔費用或雇主支付保費。文中：While employers pay the majority of this amount, the portion that workers must cover is also increasing.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To choose not to do something that you usually do or should do.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（跳躍），這裡指放棄或不去進行必要的醫療行為。文中：Because of these rising costs, many people are choosing to skip care.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause something to happen or to increase, often used for trends or prices.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 推動；導致（價格或趨勢）上升。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（駕駛），這裡指促使價格上漲。文中：which may be driving prices higher.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A sudden and significant increase in something, such as prices.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （價格或數值的）大幅跳升、暴漲。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（跳躍），這裡作名詞，形容價格的劇烈變動。文中：it would mark several years of significant price jumps.

previousArticles.title: Rising Health Insurance Costs Squeeze Workers Across the United States
previousArticles.summaryEn: Health insurance costs are rising for millions of Americans who receive coverage through their jobs. A new report from KFF shows that family premiums have reached an average of over $28,000 per year. Workers are also paying more out-of-pocket due to higher deductibles and increased premium contributions. Many employees report skipping medical care because they cannot afford the high costs. Experts warn that these financial pressures are likely to continue as medical prices and service usage grow.

quiz.question: According to the KFF survey, what has happened to the employee contribution toward family health insurance plans this year?

options.A: It has decreased as employers have taken on more of the financial burden.
options.B: It has increased by 9% compared to the previous year.
options.C: It has remained stable despite the overall rise in total insurance costs.
options.D: It has reached an average of $28,000 per year for the average worker.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，KFF 的調查明確指出員工需負擔的家庭保險費用今年上漲了 9%。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到員工負擔的部分是在增加而非減少。選項 C 錯誤，因為文中提到員工負擔的部分確實隨總成本上升。選項 D 錯誤，因為 28,000 美元是家庭保險的「總成本」，而非員工個人需負擔的金額。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided about deductibles, what can be inferred about the financial situation of workers like Joseph Babbitt?

options.A: They are likely to seek medical care more frequently because their premiums are covered.
options.B: They are financially protected from all medical costs as long as they have insurance.
options.C: They may still face significant out-of-pocket expenses even if their employer pays the monthly premiums.
options.D: They are legally required to pay for their own insurance premiums in addition to deductibles.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第三段提到，即便雇主支付了保費（premiums），但高額的自負額（deductibles）仍讓員工難以負擔醫療費用。這推論出即便有保險，員工仍需支付大筆個人支出。選項 A 與文意相反，因為高額自負額反而導致人們延誤就醫。選項 B 錯誤，因為自負額代表保險公司在達到門檻前是不會給付的。選項 D 文中並未提及法律強制規定，且文中提到有些雇主確實會支付保費。

quiz.question: In the fifth paragraph, what does the word 'limiting' most closely mean in the context of how businesses are managing rising health costs?

options.A: Expanding the variety of services available to employees.
options.B: Restricting the number of healthcare providers that employees can use.
options.C: Increasing the budget allocated for medical staff salaries.
options.D: Encouraging employees to visit more doctors for second opinions.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在第五段中，公司為了控制成本，採取了「limiting the number of doctors and hospitals」的手段，意指限制員工選擇醫療機構的範圍。選項 A 與文意完全相反。選項 C 在文中未提及，且與削減成本的目標不符。選項 D 並非限制的定義，且若限制了醫療機構的選擇，員工反而更難尋求第二意見。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the state of health insurance in the United States?

options.A: New technology like AI is the primary reason why health insurance has become more affordable for most Americans.
options.B: Employers have successfully eliminated the financial burden of healthcare for their employees through new insurance plans.
options.C: The rising costs of health insurance are creating a cycle where even insured workers struggle to access necessary medical care.
options.D: The rate of growth for insurance premiums has finally stopped, leading to a period of financial stability for families.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體主旨探討了保費與自負額不斷攀升，導致即便擁有保險的員工也因為費用過高而選擇放棄或延誤就醫，這已成為美國社會的重大問題。選項 A 與文中提到 AI 可能導致費用變高相矛盾。選項 B 與事實不符，文中強調員工負擔加重。選項 D 錯誤，文中指出雖然成長率或許放緩，但總成本依然極高，且未來預計仍會持續上漲。
